text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- BANCO DO BRASIL RECALCULATES IOF FINANCIAL TAX

Banco do Brasil will be recalculating 200 million reais worth of personal loans it made since May 5 when the higher 15-percent IOF financial tax came into force, which will result in a reduction of loans and considerable savings for clients.
-- CENBANK WILL NOT BANK ALAGOAS AND OSASCO
The federal government has decided it will not bail out Brazil's northeastern state of Alagoas and the Sao Paulo state municipality of Osasco which have defaulted on maturing bonds.
-- WORKERS PARTY TRIES TO DILUTE SCANDAL INQUIRY

The left-wing opposition Workers Party (PT) wants to dilute an inquiry into corruption allegations involving PT-run municipalities and the company Cpem by including allegations involving other political parties.
-- LOAN DEFAULTS HIT RECORD HIGH IN SAO PAULO
In May, a record 278.5 million consumers defaulted on at least one loan payment in Sao Paulo, up 57.5 percent from May 1996.
-- TRADE BALANCE HAS SMALLEST DEFICIT IN 12 MONTHS
The Brazilian trade balance showed a deficit of $271 million in May, the smallest gap in the last 12 months.
-- GOVT WILL IMPEDE ILLEGAL SALES OF CELLULAR PHONES

The Communications Ministry will place restrictions on the use of a communications system via radio, known as trunking, in order to avoid that companies in this sector offer illegal cellular phone services.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
